question: True or false: the swoosh was on shoes before the company that sold them was called Nike?
answer: True. The mark first appeared in 1971 and 1972, when the firm was Blue Ribbon Sports, an Oregon importer of Japanese running shoes; Nike was only the name of its own new shoe line. The company took Nike as its legal name in 1978. For six years the swoosh advertised a brand, not a firm.
move: A product can outgrow the company, and then the company takes its name.
trap: Assuming the logo was drawn for a company already named Nike.
reference: J. B. Strasser & Laurie Becklund, Swoosh: The Unauthorized Story of Nike and the Men Who Played There, Harcourt Brace Jovanovich, 1991
